 Print this Article 
 View Comments Derrick White and the Celtics ran away from the Bulls in a 134-99 win Monday. Danielle Parhizkaran/Globe Staff The Bulls are back in town. 
 The Celtics seek their third win at home in five days when Chicago returns to TD Garden, which will have a different look for games that are part of the NBA Cup. Friday’s game is the in-season tournament opener for both teams. 
 Boston blew out the Bulls, 134-99, on Monday behind a memorable shooting performance from Payton Pritchard. 
 Jayson Tatum added a signature highlight, beating the buzzer in overtime to clip the Nets, 125-124, on Tuesday . Tatum finished with 40 points, eight assists, and five rebounds. 
 “That was a hell of a feeling, just kind of getting back to doing things that I used to do before I was injured,” Tatum said. “And sharing that moment with my teammates on the court, seeing them rally and be excited for me.” 
 Derrick White elicited MVP chants from the Garden faithful in the win against Brooklyn. He finished with 16 points, seven assists, and five rebounds.

They know what winning basketball is and they know when guys are contributing and doing spectacular things or maybe all the little things ... I think it’s really cool and much deserved.” 
 Related : Opposing teams continue to leave Celtic Jordan Walsh wide open. He intends to make them pay. Here’s a preview of Friday’s action. 
 When: Friday, 7:30 p.m. 
 Where: TD Garden, Boston 
 TV: NBCSB. Radio: WBZ-FM 98.5. 
 Line: Boston -15. O/U: 235.5. 
 BULLS 
 Season record: 1-4. vs. spread: 2-3. Over/under: 2-1, 2 pushes 
 Last 10 games: 3-7. vs. spread: 5-5. Over/under: 3-5, 2 pushes 
 CELTICS 
 Season record: 3-1. vs. spread: 2-2. Over/under: 2-1, 1 push 
 Last 10 games: 5-5. vs. spread: 3-7. Over/under: 4-5, 1 push 
 TEAM STATISTICS 
 Points per game: Chicago 114.0, Boston 119.8 
 Points allowed per game: Chicago 130.2, Boston 111.8 
 Field goal percentage: Chicago .421, Boston .465 
 Opponent field goal percentage: Chicago .473, Boston .441 
 3-point percentage: Chicago .276, Boston .386 
 Opponent 3-point percentage: Chicago .406, Boston .345 
 Stat of the day: Chicago is 2-10 in its last 12 games against Boston. 
 Notes: The Celtics have won three straight, all of which were played at TD Garden. ... Chicago arrives in Boston following a 133-127 loss to the Knicks Wednesday. The Bulls led by as many as 19 points but could not withstand Jalen Brunson’s 38-point performance. ... Caleb Wilson, the fourth pick of the 2026 NBA Draft, is one of three rookies this season averaging at least 20 points. ... “Obviously, I have a lot of expectations put on [me] from other people, and I’m just trying to manage that and play to the best of my ability every game,” Wilson said. “I feel every game I’ve done well in some aspect. I feel every game I’m going to get better; that’s the goal. First year in the NBA, you expect some type of hardship no matter what. Just like starting a job.”
